raj_customer: Hi team — we're seeing intermittent 502s on the streaming endpoint (/v1/streams). Happens ~1-2x/hour, client sees stream cut off after ~20-40s. Request id from our app log: req_abc12345. Can someone share the minimal curl + headers you want so we can produce a reproducible trace?

emma_support: Thanks Raj — we can work through a minimal curl repro. Please attach the request id (you did) and the approximate timestamps around the failure. For cURL, we usually ask for: 1) command you ran 2) the exact Authorization token prefix (first 8 chars is fine) 3) server response headers (curl --include) and 4) --no-buffer to avoid local buffering.

raj_customer: Failure timestamps: 2026-03-16T17:02:13Z and 2026-03-16T18:15:47Z. Token prefix: sk-live-9f1a2b3c. I'll try to craft curl now.

olivia_eng: Quick tips: streaming SSE needs these headers: Accept: text/event-stream, Cache-Control: no-cache, Connection: keep-alive. Also force HTTP/1.1 with --http1.1 if you see weird chunking behavior. Example skeleton we ask customers to try:

```
curl --no-buffer --include \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Cache-Control: no-cache" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=text-gen-v3" --max-time 120
```
Add --http1.1 if proxies/nginx in path are problematic. Use -v or --trace-ascii curl-trace.txt to capture raw bytes.

emma_support: Also please run with --include so we see response headers. We want to confirm: HTTP/1.1 200 with Content-Type: text/event-stream and Transfer-Encoding: chunked. If server returns a 502, capture both the final response headers and any intermediate 5xx.

raj_customer: Here's the curl I ran (redacted token):
```
curl --no-buffer --include -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-9f1a2b3cXXXX" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Cache-Control: no-cache" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=text-gen-v3" --max-time 90
```
It returns SSE for ~30s then we get a truncated stream and client sees 502. I uploaded a debug bundle to the support portal: https://redwood.support/bundles/REQ-abc12345 (contains curl-trace.txt and app logs).

emma_support: Got the bundle, thanks. We'll pull the trace. A couple quick checks while we look: 1) can you confirm there is no intermediate proxy doing connection idle timeouts (we're looking for TCP RST in your network traces) 2) try adding --http1.1 as Olivia suggested and see if the behavior changes.

olivia_eng: If you can run a local tcpdump while reproducing, filter on the client IP: tcpdump -w sse-req.pcap host <client-ip> and share. Also grep the logs we kept: `grep req_abc12345 /var/log/redwood/streams.log` — want to see server-side lifecycle for that request id.

raj_customer: Ran with --http1.1, same behavior. Uploaded pcap to the bundle. Logs show:
```
[17:02:13Z] req=req_abc12345 stream_open model=text-gen-v3
[17:02:43Z] req=req_abc12345 stream_chunk_sent token_count=386
[17:02:43Z] req=req_abc12345 stream_closed reason=backend_read_error status=502 trace=trace-778899
```
mike_support: We reproduced locally using your curl command and the trace you provided — confirmed chunked body then backend read error at ~30s. For next steps we will: 1) escalate to runtime team with trace id trace-778899 2) try a fallback to text-gen-v2-small to see if it's model-specific. In the meantime, can you try adding the header `Connection: keep-alive` explicitly? Some client libs strip it.

emma_support: Also try `--no-keepalive` on curl? Actually curl has --no-keepalive to disable; we want keep-alive so don't use that. Try explicitly: -H "Connection: keep-alive".

raj_customer: Tried with Connection: keep-alive and same result (uploaded updated curl-trace). One additional data point: when we hit a 502, the server response headers included `Server: nginx/1.22.0` then a 502 body with HTML (looks like proxy layer).

mike_support: That's useful — proxy layer likely raising 502 after upstream closed. Runtime team will check upstream timeouts and the model worker logs for trace-778899. For immediate mitigation, you can enable model fallback in your route config to a smaller variant so you avoid the worker kernel path that might hit the bug: route "streams" -> fallback_models: ["text-gen-v2-small"]. I pushed a canary rule for your org to allow fallback for 1 hour. :thumbsup:

raj_customer: Thank you — trying fallback now. If it stabilizes I'll mark resolved. Appreciate the quick triage.

emma_support: Closing loop: we've attached the runtime investigation ticket ID: RT-5423 and included your bundle. If you see recurrence after fallback, please reopen this thread or ping on-call. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: alert: spike of 502s on /v1/streams at 2026-03-16T17:02:40Z (15 spikes in 1h) — ticket RT-5423 created.

raj_customer: Looks stable with fallback for now. Will report back if it reappears. Thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
